articles.title: Leeds defeat Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge
articles.summary: Noah Okafor scored twice to secure Leeds United's first victory at Chelsea in 27 years with an impressive 4-1 win at Stamford Bridge. The result moves Leeds up to sixth place in the Premier League table, while deepening the pressure on Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso following a disappointing home performance.

articles.title: Arsenal extend lead after draw with Newcastle
articles.summary: Noni Madueke scored a crucial second-half goal to earn Arsenal a 2-2 draw against Newcastle United at St James' Park. Despite the entertaining and hard-fought stalemate, the reigning Premier League champions extended their lead at the top of the table to six points.

articles.title: Teenager Williams-Barnett inspires Spurs win
articles.summary: Tottenham Hotspur teenager Luca Williams-Barnett starred for Roberto de Zerbi's side, delivering a remarkable performance in their comfortable victory over Ipswich Town. The young player made a significant impact on his full Premier League debut, helping his team secure another important win.

articles.title: Late own goal sinks Palace in Frank's debut
articles.summary: A late Dwight McNeil own goal in the 85th minute handed Coventry City a 3-2 victory over Crystal Palace. The result moves Coventry three points clear of the relegation zone, while ruining Thomas Frank's first match in charge of Palace, who remain at the bottom of the table.

articles.title: Anderson volley earns Man City draw
articles.summary: Elliot Anderson scored a fantastic volley to help Manchester City come from behind and secure a 1-1 draw against Fulham. The point prevents another defeat for City, earning them their first Premier League point in over a month after a difficult run of results.

articles.title: Evanilson scores again in Bournemouth win
articles.summary: Evanilson scored in his sixth consecutive Premier League match to help Bournemouth defeat Nottingham Forest 2-0 at the Vitality Stadium. The in-form striker's opening goal set the tone for another victory, lifting Bournemouth to fourth place in the league table.

articles.title: Sunderland hold Aston Villa to scoreless draw
articles.summary: Aston Villa's ongoing struggles at home continued as they were held to a frustrating goalless draw by Sunderland in the Premier League. Unai Emery's side failed to break down a dogged visiting defence, resulting in a stalemate at Villa Park.

articles.title: Madueke secures Arsenal draw against Newcastle
articles.summary: Arsenal secured a 2-2 draw against Newcastle United at St James' Park under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. Noni Madueke's second-half strike rescued a point for Mikel Arteta's side after an overwhelmed Newcastle fought back valiantly, though the match also saw David Raya pick up an injury.

articles.title: Alonso admits fragile Chelsea must improve
articles.summary: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso admitted his side is too fragile after suffering a humiliating 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United. The result leaves Chelsea eighth in the Premier League and having lost more games than Manchester United, raising serious concerns about their prospects of qualifying for European football.

articles.title: Coventry edge Palace to ruin Frank debut
articles.summary: Crystal Palace remained bottom of the Premier League table after a 3-2 defeat to Coventry City ruined Thomas Frank's first game in charge. Despite showing moments of promise and twice equalizing, familiar defensive failings cost Palace dearly as an 85th-minute own goal sealed their fifth consecutive league defeat.

articles.title: Williams-Barnett stars in Tottenham win
articles.summary: Luca Williams-Barnett became Tottenham's youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 during an impressive full debut against Ipswich Town. The 18-year-old academy star scored and provided an assist for Dominic Solanke, driving Roberto De Zerbi's side to their fourth victory in five league matches.

articles.title: Bournemouth defeat Forest for ninth straight win
articles.summary: Evanilson and Justin Kluivert secured a 2-0 victory for Bournemouth against Nottingham Forest, extending their club-record winning run to nine matches in all competitions. Evanilson's opening goal was his sixth in consecutive league games, lifting Marco Rose's side into fourth place in the standings.

articles.title: Celtic sweep St Mirren aside in Premiership
articles.summary: Celtic strengthened their grip at the top of the Scottish Premiership with a comfortable 4-1 victory over St Mirren. Goals from Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan, and Camilo Duran helped the champions overcome the absences of injured midfielders to secure another commanding three points.

articles.title: Lazio extend Serie A lead with Lecce win
articles.summary: Lazio extended their lead at the top of Serie A to four points with a comfortable 3-0 home victory over Lecce. Tijjani Noslin scored twice, and Davide Frattesi added a late goal to keep Gennaro Gattuso's side unbeaten and secure their tenth victory in twelve matches.

articles.title: Musk's lawyer joins Brady in Chelsea bid
articles.summary: Alex Spiro, a lawyer representing Elon Musk, is reportedly in discussions to buy a stake in Chelsea by investing in majority owners Clearlake Capital. This development follows news that former NFL star Tom Brady is also in talks to purchase a minority shareholding at Stamford Bridge.

articles.title: Sunderland hold Aston Villa to stalemate
articles.summary: Aston Villa were held to a frustrating 0-0 draw at home by a dogged Sunderland side. Unai Emery's team struggled to break down the visitors' resolute defense, managing only one shot on target from inside the penalty box during a painful stalemate at Villa Park.

articles.title: Fulham hold struggling Manchester City to draw
articles.summary: Manchester City ended a three-game losing run in the Premier League but were held to a passive 1-1 draw by Fulham at home. Elliot Anderson's goal rescued a point for City after Rodrigo Muniz opened the scoring, leaving home fans to voice their frustration with boos at the whistle.

articles.title: Keating denies Chelsea in scoreless WSL draw
articles.summary: Goalkeeper Khiara Keating produced a resilient performance to help Liverpool hold Women's Super League leaders Chelsea to a goalless draw. Gareth Taylor's Liverpool side successfully frustrated Chelsea, who were missing key players such as the injured Melvine Malard and Lauren James.

articles.title: Newcastle end Arsenal's winning run in draw
articles.summary: Newcastle United ended Arsenal's four-match winning streak without conceding by holding the league leaders to a frantic 2-2 draw. The hard-fought contest at St James' Park saw both teams battle intensely as Arsenal fought to maintain their advantage at the summit.

articles.title: Erasmus proceeds with online watchalong
articles.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus went ahead with hosting an online watchalong during his team's match against Ireland in the Nations Championship. The event took place despite potential risks concerning his ongoing World Rugby disciplinary directives.

articles.title: Alcaraz reaches final after comeback win
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz displayed resilience to fight back from a set down against Ben Shelton, securing his place in the final of the ATP Finals in Turin through an impressive and hard-fought victory.

articles.title: Frick wins first match as Aberdeen boss
articles.summary: Mario Frick enjoyed a dream start to his tenure as Aberdeen manager, guiding his new team to a thrilling 4-2 victory away against Kilmarnock in a six-goal encounter.

articles.title: Ireland seal narrow victory over South Africa
articles.summary: Robert Baloucoune scored a crucial brace of tries to help Ireland secure a tense 20-17 victory against South Africa in the Nations Championship.

articles.title: Bournemouth defeat Forest to make history
articles.summary: Bournemouth continued their exceptional run of form with a comfortable 2-0 victory over Nottingham Forest, setting multiple club records in the process under manager Marco Rose.
